Nail Fungus Recovery Calling Playbook
Everything a Logicall agent needs to start placing high-intent recovery calls for
ZoliraRx — the product, the per-stage scripts, the objections, and the compliance
lines that matter most in this category.

Executive Summary
01
This vertical launches ZoliraRx — a physician-prescribed topical compound for toenail fungus
(onychomycosis). Unlike the ED funnel, dosage and checkout are two separate pages here, so
Logicall handles two recoverable stages for this brand: Dosage Abandon and Checkout
Abandon.
STAGE PRIORITY — CHECKOUT ABANDON IS THE BIGGEST LEVER
Page 1 of 10

The two stages don't carry the same weight. Checkout Abandon has the lowest volume but the
highest conversion ceiling: the lead already chose a package, reached the payment page, and
stopped one click short. They're the closest to "yes" of any segment here. Treat every
Checkout Abandon call as priority.
IMPORTANT — QUIZ ABANDONMENT IS NOT RECOVERABLE
The assessment is long (36 screens) and captures name, email and phone near the very end
— the "Contact Info" screen sits two screens before the finish. If a lead drops before that, we
have zero contact data. There is no "Quiz Abandon" recovery. The recoverable stages start
once a lead finishes the assessment and lands on the package page.
The two recoverable stages
1. Dosage Abandon — finished the assessment, saw the four packages, didn't pick one.
(Pricing-active call.)
2. Checkout Abandon — picked a package, reached checkout, didn't complete the order.
(Pricing-active call.)
What's different about this category
It's topical, not a pill. A brush-on prescription applied to the nail — not an oral drug. That
single fact answers a large share of the objections you'll hear.
The timeline is long, and honest. A toenail takes roughly 9–12 months to fully grow out.
The medication doesn't clear the nail they have — the clear nail grows in from the base. That
reality is your strongest argument for the longer packages.
Shame is the real barrier. Most of these leads have hidden their feet for years and never
showed a doctor. Warm, matter-of-fact, zero judgment — same posture as the ED vertical.
Four packages. More plan choice than any other Standard Meds funnel, which is exactly
why "which one do I pick?" is the number-one Dosage Abandon objection.
The Product at a Glance
02
Read this card before your first call. Everything you'll anchor on lives here.
ZoliraRx
TOENAIL FUNGUS · TOPICAL · ITRACONAZOLE 1% + TERBINAFINE 1% WITH DMSO
Page 2 of 10

A physician-prescribed topical compound combining two prescription antifungals — Itraconazole
1% and Terbinafine 1% — in a DMSO carrier. Brushed onto the affected nail, typically at bedtime.
Compounded at an FDA-registered pharmacy.
MECHANISM Itraconazole and terbinafine attack the fungus through two different pathways. The
hard part has never been the antifungals — it's getting them through the nail plate,
which is dense and naturally close to impermeable. DMSO is the carrier that solves
the penetration problem, dispersing the actives through the nail to where the
fungus actually lives.
VS. PILLS Oral antifungals flood the whole system and typically require liver monitoring and
blood work. ZoliraRx is applied directly to the nail, so systemic exposure is
minimized — no blood tests. This is the single biggest reason patients choose it.
TIMELINE Clear nail grows in from the base. Patients typically report the yellowing starting to
fade around weeks 3–4 and visible clear nail at the base around week 6, with a full
toenail grow-out taking 9–12 months.
AUTHORITY A licensed physician reviews every assessment. Compounded at an FDA-registered
pharmacy.
GUARANTEE 90-day money-back guarantee.
TONE Practical, reassuring, zero judgment. "It's a brush-on prescription — no pills, no
blood tests, and nobody has to look at your feet."

Anchor on the 12-month, step down to the 6-month. This isn't a pricing trick — it's the clinical reality. A
toenail grows out over 9–12 months, so the 12-month plan is the only one that covers a full grow-out, and it's
less than half the per-month cost of the single month. If a year is too big a commitment, the 6-month at $69/mo
is your step-down. The page marks the 3-month "Most Popular" and pre-selects it, so plenty of leads land there
— take the sale, don't fight it.
OFFERS MAY VARY OVER TIME
Standard Meds continuously tests and rotates offers, so a lead may see plans or prices
different from the ones above. The live dosage/checkout page is always the source of truth.
Per-Stage Playbook
03
Two stages, two cards. Openers and discovery questions are a guide, not a script to read
verbatim — adjust to your own voice. Throughout: this is a category people are embarrassed
about. Warm and matter-of-fact beats enthusiastic.
STAGE 1 OF 2
Dosage Abandon
The lead finished the 36-screen assessment, landed on the package page, saw the four options,
and didn't pick one. They invested real time and stopped one decision short. With four options
in front of them, the objection is almost never "tell me about the product" — it's "which one do
I pick" or "is it worth it."
GOAL
Send the package page via SMS
AVG CALL
≤ 5 min
PRICING POSTURE
Active — anchor 12mo, step down to 6mo
OPENER (≤ 15 SEC)

nail health assessment recently and I saw you got all the way to the package page but

came up?"
ADDRESS — MOST COMMON PATTERNS
"Wasn't sure which package to pick" → the one you'll hear most. Answer with the
nail, not the discount: "a toenail takes about nine to twelve months to fully grow out
— the medication doesn't clear the nail you have, the clear nail grows in from the
base. So the twelve-month at forty-nine dollars a month is the one that covers a full
grow-out, and it's less than half the monthly price of the single month. If that's a
bigger commitment than you want right now, the six-month at sixty-nine is the
sensible middle."
"Price / is it worth it" → per-month math plus the comparison to the alternatives
(below), then the 90-day money-back guarantee.
"I don't want to be charged before I know I'm approved" → "You're not. The total
due at checkout is zero — you're only charged if the physician approves your

"Wanted to think about it" → acknowledge, offer to send the link so they can revisit
with everything in front of them.

STAGE 2 OF 2 · HIGHEST PRIORITY
Checkout Abandon
Lower volume than Dosage but the single highest-conversion call in the playbook. The lead
picked a package, reached the payment page, and stopped one click before placing the order.
Something specific stopped them — usually price hesitation, payment friction, a last-minute "let
me think," or confusion about the pharmacy name on the order summary. They're already
informed and already convinced enough to get their card out. Don't re-sell from scratch — just
remove the friction.

Objection Library
04
The full bench of rebuttals — guidance, not scripts to read verbatim. When a question turns
medical (dosing, interactions, liver or kidney conditions, whether it's safe with their other
medication), defer to the physician review — do not advise.
Q "I've tried everything — nothing works on nail fungus."
Page 7 of 10

A "You're right that most of it doesn't, and there's a specific reason. The nail plate is dense and close to
impermeable — drugstore products just sit on top and never reach the fungus underneath. The
difference here isn't the antifungals, it's the DMSO carrier that disperses them through the nail to where
the fungus actually lives. That's the part the products you already tried were missing."
Q "Isn't there a pill for this? Why a topical?"
A "There is, and a lot of patients specifically don't want it — oral antifungals go through your whole
system and generally come with liver monitoring and blood work. This is applied directly to the nail, so
systemic exposure is minimized and there's no blood test regimen. For most people that's the whole
appeal. Your physician reviews your assessment and will tell you if a topical is the right approach for
you."
Q "How long until I see results?"
A "I want to be straight with you, because this is where people get disappointed with anything they try:
the medication doesn't clear the nail you already have — the clear nail grows in from the base. Patients
often see the yellowing start to fade in the first month and clear nail at the base around week six. A full
toenail takes about nine to twelve months to grow out completely. That's not this product being slow,
that's how nails grow — and it's exactly why the longer packages exist."
Q "Which package should I get?"
A "Match it to the grow-out. Twelve months at forty-nine dollars a month covers a full nail cycle and it's
the lowest per-month price we have — less than half the single month. Six months at sixty-nine is the
middle if a year feels like a lot. Three months at seventy-nine is what most people start with. The single
month at $129 works if you want to try it first, but you'd be re-ordering before you see the finish line, and
it costs the most per month."
Q "It's too expensive."
A "Completely fair — let's put it next to the alternatives. Podiatrist visits run two to four hundred dollars
each and this takes months. Oral antifungals are three to eight hundred plus the lab work. Laser is five
hundred to fifteen hundred with no guarantee. And most people have already spent a few hundred over
the years on drugstore products that couldn't get through the nail. The twelve-month here is $588 total
— about forty-nine a month — and it includes the doctor consultation, unlimited doctor support and
overnight shipping at no extra cost, with a 90-day money-back guarantee."
Q "Am I being charged right now?"
A "No. The checkout total reads zero due now — your card is on file, but you're only charged once a
licensed physician reviews your assessment and approves the prescription. If it isn't approved, you're
not charged."
Q "Who is ChemistryRx? I thought I was buying ZoliraRx."
A "Same product — ChemistryRx is the FDA-registered compounding pharmacy that makes it, so it
shows up on the order line with the pharmacy name and the formula. ZoliraRx is the Standard Meds
program name for the same itraconazole-and-terbinafine-with-DMSO compound. Nothing changed
between the page you were on and the checkout."
Page 8 of 10

Q "How do I know this isn't a scam?"
A "Fair question. This is a real compounded prescription — a licensed physician reviews your assessment
before anything is prescribed, it's compounded at an FDA-registered pharmacy, and you're not charged
unless it's approved. There's also a 90-day money-back guarantee."
Q "Is DMSO safe? I've only seen it sold for horses."
A "It has a reputation from the veterinary and industrial world, but DMSO has decades of medical
research behind it and is FDA-approved for other medical uses. What we use is prescription grade, and
it's here for one job: carrying the antifungals through the nail. The physician reviews your assessment
before any of it is prescribed."
Q "Does insurance cover it?"
A "This is a cash-pay compounded telehealth program, so it doesn't go through insurance — which is
what keeps it private and lets the pharmacy compound this specific formula. It's one straightforward
price and you can cancel anytime."
Q "I'd be embarrassed to show my feet to a doctor."
A "You don't have to — and honestly, that's the reason most people put this off for years. The whole
assessment happens online, the physician reviews it remotely, and it ships to your door in plain
packaging. Nobody has to look at your feet."
Q "I need to ask my doctor first."
A "Of course — and a licensed physician is part of this: they review your health assessment before
anything is approved and will flag anything that isn't a fit. If it helps, I can send you the link so you have
all the details in front of you for that conversation."
Q "I'm on other medication / I have liver problems — is this safe for me?"
A "That's an important question, and it's exactly what the physician reviews in your assessment before
anything is approved. I'm not able to give medical advice on that, but the review is built to catch it."
Compliance & Operational Rules
05
The universal rules from your first Standard Meds playbook still apply in full — TCPA window,
self-identification, recording disclosure, opt-out, no invented discounts, no claiming approval
before physician review, no link-send to voicemail. This section covers only what's different or
elevated for nail fungus.
#1 RULE — THIS SEGMENT SKEWS OLDER AND MEDICATED
Nail fungus leads are disproportionately 55+ and many are already on other prescriptions, with
liver or kidney conditions in the mix. You are never to assess, advise on, or reassure a patient
Page 9 of 10

about any drug interaction, liver/kidney risk, or dosing question. Every such question routes to
one answer: "the physician reviews that in your assessment before anything is approved." This
protects the patient and it protects the program.
New or elevated for nail fungus
Never advise on interactions or liver/kidney risk
Any "is this safe with X" question → "the physician reviews that." Do not reassure with a yes. See the red
callout above.
Never promise a timeline beyond §2
No "your nail will be clear in three months." The honest line is the grow-out: fading in the first month, clear
nail at the base around week six, full grow-out in 9–12 months. Never diagnose from a description of their
nail.
Never build a pitch on the checkout countdown
The checkout page runs its own timer. Don't use it. If you need urgency, use the medical reality: "the nail
grows about a millimetre a month — every month you wait is a month added to the finish line."
Stay discreet & non-judgmental
These leads have hidden their feet for years. Professional, matter-of-fact tone. Never make the patient
feel awkward about the topic — it costs the call.
Use the right checkout host
buy-fungus.standardmeds.com , not buy.standardmeds.com . Sending the wrong host means the lead's
cart won't load and the recovery is lost.
Lead with "you're not charged today"
It's true, it's on the page, and it removes the biggest hesitation in the category. Use it before you reach for
a smaller package.
